correction.text: the 1919 shape borrowed for the last weeks of 1918; unverified

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1919 while the Hungarian Democratic Republic was proclaimed in 1918. Unverified: page budget. Which of Slovakia, Carpathian Ruthenia, Transylvania and Croatia were still Hungarian-held in the last weeks of 1918 is on none of the pages opened; the 1919 shape is borrowed.

correction.text: the post-Trianon rump (about 92,000 km2) for 1919, with the Slovak zone of June 1919 as a contest and the Romanian-held land hatched

keyframe_review.note: 119,603 km2, 1.3 times the 92,833 km2 of the infobox (1920), and its bounding box reaches into Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia. The pages show Hungarian forces in the north only between mid-June and the cease-fire of 1 July 1919 ('after Hungarian forces had advanced into Slovakia', Slovak Soviet Republic of 16 June), while the Romanian army held Hungary east of the Tisza from 1 May and Budapest from 4 August. For the year the stable core is the post-Trianon rump; draw the 1920 shape and add the June Slovak contest and the Romanian occupation from the ledger. [Fix pass after review eu-21-b: the Romanian contest and occupation drawn from the ledger now lie in Hungary east of the Tisza and across the post-Trianon territory minus the Lake Balaton area, not in Slovakia and Ruthenia.]

92,074 km2 against the infobox's 92,833 km2 (1920) and 93,073 km2 (1930; the Trianon page: 'a landlocked state of 93,073 square kilometres'): ratio 0.99. Trianon (signed 4 June 1920, in force 26 July 1921) left Hungary with about 28% of the pre-war land; Burgenland went to Austria in 1921, Sopron stayed after the December 1921 plebiscite. The shape holds to 1937.

107,368 km2, +15,294 km2 on 1937. The First Vienna Award page gives 'Slovakia lost 10,390 km2 with 854,277 inhabitants' and calls 14,106 km2 Hungary's original demand; no figure for the Ruthenian part. The shape is closer to the demand than to the award, so it may overstate by a few thousand km2; within a factor of two.

122,186 km2, +14,818 km2 on 1938: Carpathian Ruthenia occupied 15-18 March 1939 and, after the short Slovak-Hungarian War, 1,897 km2 (69,630 people) of eastern Slovakia (negotiations 27 March - 4 April). The Kingdom page: 'occupied and annexed the remainder of the Carpatho-Ukraine'.
122,164 km2: the state before the Second Vienna Award of 30 August 1940, which added Northern Transylvania (43,104 km2); that gain is in the ledger with its month and the 1941 shape holds it.
174,011 km2 against the infobox's 172,149 km2 (1941): ratio 1.01. Holds Northern Transylvania and the Yugoslav land annexed in 1941 (Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje, Prekmurje).
Same extent as 1941-1942 (174,011 km2); no territorial event on the pages between 1941 and the German occupation of 19 March 1944.

correction.text: the 1943 shape, German-occupied from 19 March 1944; Northern Transylvania lost in October

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1943 although the state lasted to 1 February 1946. For 1944 the extent is that of 1943 until October, when Northern Transylvania passed to Romanian and Soviet control after the Battle of Carei (25 October 1944, Vienna Award page). The Germans occupied the country from 19 March 1944 ('On 19 March 1944, the Germans responded by invading Hungary'). [Fix pass: Backa and Baranja also left Hungary in October 1944 (ledger, Partisans); the 1943 outline is kept for the year as a snapshot, and the ledger carries the 1944 changes with their months.]

correction.text: Hungary within the frontier of 1 January 1938

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1945-1946, which Cliopatria lacks. The Paris peace treaty of 10 February 1947 set the frontier 'as it existed on January 1, 1938' except for three villages south of Bratislava and declared the Vienna Award 'null and void'. The page does not date the de facto return of southern Slovakia, Ruthenia and Backa; the lines of 1937 are used from 1945.

region.text: Hungary

ledger.note: 1918: Hungary leaves the Dual Monarchy as the Hungarian Democratic Republic. 'the Hungarian Democratic Republic and then the Hungarian Soviet Republic were briefly proclaimed in 1918 and 1919' (the page gives years only). The state continues as a kingdom without a king from 1920.

21 March 1919: the Hungarian Soviet Republic is proclaimed. 'The Republic was proclaimed after the 21 March 1919 coup.' It falls in August ('On 2 August, Kun fled Hungary towards the Austrian border').

region.text: 'the entire east bank of the Tisza River' (the page's words for 1 May 1919): the Hungarian counties Hajdu-Bihar, Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg and Bekes inside the 1920 frontier (Debrecen taken on 23 April, Bekescsaba on 25-26 April); the parts of Csongrad and Jasz-Nagykun-Szolnok east of the river are not drawn; the county names are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 16 April 1919: the Romanian offensive begins ('The Romanian offensive began on 16 April 1919'); 'By the evening of 1 May, the entire east bank of the Tisza River was under the control of the Romanian Army.' [Fix pass after review eu-21-b, 2026-11-01: the region was drawn in Slovakia and Ruthenia (1919 shape minus 1920 shape); it is now the land the Hungarian-Romanian War page names, re-read on the page: 'On the evening of 1 May, the entire east bank of the Tisza River was under the control of the Romanian Army'; 'Romania occupied all of Hungary except for an area around Lake Balaton'; 'In early 1920, Romanian troops departed Hungary'.]

region.text: parts of the north of Czechoslovakia taken by the Hungarian Red Army, Presov where the Slovak Soviet Republic was declared on 16 June 1919

ledger.note: Mid-June 1919: the Hungarian Red Army advances into the north. 'the communists immediately declared the establishment of the Slovak Soviet Republic' in Presov on 16 June 1919 'after Hungarian forces had advanced into Slovakia' (Hungarian-Romanian War page); the Trianon page: 'The Hungarian Red Army pushed Czechoslovak troops out of parts of the north in 1919'. The start month is the 16 June declaration; the campaign began earlier.

region.text: parts of the north of Czechoslovakia taken by the Hungarian Red Army, Presov where the Slovak Soviet Republic was declared on 16 June 1919

region.text: 'the entire east bank of the Tisza River' (the page's words for 1 May 1919): the Hungarian counties Hajdu-Bihar, Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg and Bekes inside the 1920 frontier (Debrecen taken on 23 April, Bekescsaba on 25-26 April); the parts of Csongrad and Jasz-Nagykun-Szolnok east of the river are not drawn; the county names are the researcher's reading

29 February 1920: the monarchy is restored without a king. 'On 29 February 1920, a coalition of right-wing political forces united and returned Hungary' to a kingdom; Miklos Horthy 'was chosen for this position [regent] on 1 March'.

region.text: the whole of Transylvania and central parts of Banat

ledger.note: 4 June 1920: Trianon gives Transylvania and central Banat to Romania ('Romania gained all of Transylvania'; 'the whole of Transylvania was taken by Romania' on the Kingdom page). Romania had declared the union on 1 December 1918, so the Hungarian shapes of 1919 onward never contain it. Crisana and Maramures are not named on the page. Signed 4 June 1920, ratified by Hungary 16 November 1920, in force 26 July 1921.

region.text: Croatia-Slavonia, Medjimurje, Banat, Backa and Baranja, and two-thirds of the Slovene March (Prekmurje)

ledger.note: 4 June 1920: Trianon gives the south to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes: 'Croatia-Slavonia, Medjimurje, Banat, Backa and Baranja, and two-thirds of the Slovene March (Prekmurje)'. 'Pecs, Mohacs, Baja and Szigetvar were assigned to Hungary.' Region is the researcher's reading of the names; Croatia proper (Croatia-Slavonia) is approximated by Slavonia.

region.text: Slovakia (Upper Hungary) and Carpathian Ruthenia

ledger.note: 4 June 1920: Trianon confirms Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia for Czechoslovakia. 'Carpathian Ruthenia went to Czechoslovakia under the Treaty of Saint-Germain in 1919'; Czechoslovak troops had held Ruthenia from April 1919 (Czechoslovak dossier).

region.text: most of Burgenland

ledger.note: 1921: Burgenland passes to Austria. The Trianon page gives Austria 'Most of Burgenland' and adds that 'the district of Sopron opted to remain within Hungary after a plebiscite held in December 1921'; the treaty came into force on 26 July 1921. The Austrian dossier dates its gain to 1921 from its own page.

region.text: the territories in southern Slovakia and southern Carpathian Ruthenia, Kosice, Uzhhorod and Mukachevo among the towns

ledger.note: 2 November 1938: the First Vienna Award gives Hungary the south of Slovakia and Ruthenia. 'Czechoslovakia had to surrender the territories in southern Slovakia and southern Carpathian Ruthenia'; 'Slovakia lost 10,390 km2 with 854,277 inhabitants'; the Royal Hungarian Army occupied them 'between November 5 and 10, 1938'.

region.text: 1,897 km2 of eastern Slovakia

ledger.note: March 1939: the short Slovak-Hungarian War. The page says only 'After a short Slovak-Hungarian War' and does not date the fighting; the Slovak state needs its own dossier. [Reviewer eu-21-b, 2026-11-01: the First Vienna Award page does date the start: Hungary 'on March 23 launched a larger attack on eastern Slovakia'; month set to 3 and confidence raised to 2.]

region.text: the remainder of Carpatho-Ukraine

ledger.note: 15-18 March 1939: Hungary occupies Carpathian Ruthenia. 'between March 15 and 18, it was occupied by Hungary', after the region declared independence as Carpatho-Ukraine on 14-15 March; the Kingdom page: 'occupied and annexed the remainder of the Carpatho-Ukraine'.

region.text: 1,897 km2 of eastern Slovakia

ledger.note: 4 April 1939: the fighting ends in a settlement. 'the March 27-April 4 negotiations gave Hungary 1,897 km2 with 69,630 inhabitants in eastern Slovakia.'

region.text: 1,897 km2 with 69,630 inhabitants in eastern Slovakia

ledger.note: April 1939: eastern Slovakia (1,897 km2) goes to Hungary after the Slovak-Hungarian War ('the March 27-April 4 negotiations gave Hungary 1,897 km2 with 69,630 inhabitants in eastern Slovakia').

region.text: Northern Transylvania, all of Maramures and part of Crisana (43,104 km2)

ledger.note: 30 August 1940: the Second Vienna Award gives Hungary Northern Transylvania. 'they assigned the territory of Northern Transylvania' (43,104 km2, 2,578,100 inhabitants in 1941); 'The Hungarian troops stepped across the Trianon borders on 5 September' and 'reached the pre-Trianon border' on 13 September.

region.text: Backa (Vojvodina), Baranja, Medjimurje (Murakoz) and the north-eastern Prekmurje

ledger.note: April 1941: Hungary joins the invasion of Yugoslavia (begun 6 April; capitulation 17 April) and annexes the north. Hungary 'occupied and subsequently annexed Vojvodina, Baranja, Backa and Medjimurje' and 'the northeastern Prekmurje region' (no date on the page); the Kingdom page: 'allowed to annex the Backa (Backa) region in Vojvodina'. [Fix pass: the Hungarian occupation page gives 'The occupation began on 11 April 1941 when 80,000 Hungarian troops crossed the Yugoslav border' and 'Annexed by Hungary: 14 December 1941' for Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje and Prekmurje. The gain is dated to the occupation (April, the control the shapes show for the year); the formal incorporation was 14 December. Confidence 2 because the two dates differ.]

region.text: the whole country

ledger.note: 19 March 1944: Germany occupies Hungary. 'On 19 March 1944, the Germans responded by invading Hungary'; the government stays in place until October.

region.text: the whole country as of 1943: the Red Army's campaign took Northern Transylvania, Ruthenia, Backa and Hungary proper between September 1944 and April 1945

ledger.note: September 1944: the Red Army enters Hungary. 'In September 1944, Soviet forces crossed the Hungarian border.' 'The Soviets and Romanians completed the encirclement of Budapest on 29 December 1944.' The German and Hungarian units in Budapest 'surrendered on 13 February 1945'. An armistice was signed in Moscow on 20 January 1945 by the Miklos provisional government ('On 20 January 1945, representatives of the Miklos provisional government signed an armistice in Moscow').
October 1944: the Arrow Cross takes power. 'in October, German forces overthrew Horthy and Lakatos and installed a puppet regime' (Szalasi, 1944-1945).

region.text: Northern Transylvania, all of Maramures and part of Crisana (43,104 km2)

ledger.note: 25 October 1944: Northern Transylvania is lost again. The armistice of 12 September 1944 declared the Vienna Award void; 'After the Battle of Carei on 25 October 1944, all of Northern Transylvania was under Romanian and Soviet control' (Soviet administration to 9 March 1945).

region.text: Backa and Baranja, annexed in 1941

ledger.note: October 1944: Backa and Baranja leave Hungary. The Hungarian occupation page: Soviet troops captured the area in October 1944, the Red Army withdrew after a few weeks and 'ceded full control of the region to the Partisans'; 'Backa and Baranja were restored to Yugoslav control' (late 1944), with a Partisan military administration set up on 17 October 1944. The counterpart is the Partisan movement, which was the Yugoslav authority before the March 1945 merge (the Democratic Federal Yugoslavia page, earlier source of this event, says 'Backa was reannexed by Hungary (1941-1944)'). The yugoslav-partisans dossier does not yet book this land (routed to the orchestrator).

region.text: southern Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia, the land of the First Vienna Award and of March 1939

ledger.note: 1945: southern Slovakia and Ruthenia revert. Bridging a silence: the page gives only that the 1947 treaty 'declared the Vienna Award null and void' and set the frontier 'as it existed on January 1, 1938'; the date of the de facto return is not on it. [Fix pass: the Hungary in World War II page (read 2026-11-01) says only that the Vienna Award was declared 'null and void' by the 1947 treaty and that the Red Army entered Hungary in September 1944; it dates no return of southern Slovakia and Ruthenia, so the year stays a bridge. The czechoslovakia dossier books the strip from slovak-republic, not from here (routed to the orchestrator).]

region.text: Medjimurje and Prekmurje, annexed in 1941

ledger.note: 1945: Medjimurje and Prekmurje leave Hungary. The Hungarian occupation page: 'Medjimurje and Prekmurje remained occupied until the last weeks of the war'; no exact date. The counterpart is yugoslavia because the Partisans and the exile government had merged in March 1945 (yugoslavia/ledger merge).

region.text: the whole country

ledger.note: 4 April 1945: the German occupation ends with the Soviet advance. The Hungary in World War II page: 'Officially, Soviet operations in Hungary ended on 4 April 1945, when the last German troops were expelled' (Budapest had surrendered on 13 February 1945). Earlier this event was bridged at confidence 1 to 1945; the nazi-germany dossier gives May 1945 for its own end of the occupation.

region.text: the whole country as of 1943

ledger.note: 4 April 1945: the fighting in Hungary ends. 'Officially, Soviet operations in Hungary ended on 4 April 1945, when the last German troops were expelled.'

region.text: Hungary within the frontier of 1 January 1938, under Soviet occupation

ledger.note: From April 1945 Hungary is held by the Red Army. The Kingdom page: 'Under Soviet occupation, the fate of the Kingdom of Hungary was already determined'; the Hungary in World War II page has the Provisional National Government as a 'temporary semi-independent government' under Soviet supervision after the war in Hungary ended on 4 April 1945. Neither page dates the start of the occupation or names the Allied Control Commission, so April 1945 (end of the fighting) is a bridge and the land is the frontier of 1 January 1938. The occupation continues in the second-hungarian-republic dossier.

region.text: Hungary within the frontier of 1 January 1938

ledger.note: 1 February 1946: the monarchy is abolished; the Soviet occupation does not end but passes to the Second Hungarian Republic (second-hungarian-republic), so this end only closes the pair for this dossier.

region.text: the Kingdom of Hungary within the frontier of 1 January 1938

ledger.note: 1 February 1946: the monarchy is abolished and the Second Hungarian Republic begins. 'until the monarchy was formally abolished on 1 February 1946'; 'The regency was replaced by the Second Hungarian Republic'.

wars.name: Hungarian-Romanian War

zones.text: 'the entire east bank of the Tisza River' (the page's words for 1 May 1919): the Hungarian counties Hajdu-Bihar, Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg and Bekes inside the 1920 frontier (Debrecen taken on 23 April, Bekescsaba on 25-26 April); the parts of Csongrad and Jasz-Nagykun-Szolnok east of the river are not drawn; the county names are the researcher's reading
'all of Hungary except for an area around Lake Balaton': the post-Trianon territory minus a 60 km disc at Lake Balaton (the disc is the researcher's reading of 'an area around Lake Balaton')

wars.outcome: Romanian victory: the Romanian army crossed the Tisza on 29-30 July 1919 and held Budapest from 4 August; it left in early 1920, and Trianon fixed Hungary's eastern frontier.
wars.note: The page dates the war 13 November 1918 - 3 August 1919; the Romanian offensive began on 16 April 1919. Zones corrected in the fix pass: the contested land is the east bank of the Tisza (first zone) and the occupied land is Hungary except the Lake Balaton area (second zone); the earlier zone fell in Slovakia and Ruthenia.

wars.name: Hungarian-Czechoslovak War

zones.text: parts of the north of Czechoslovakia taken by the Hungarian Red Army, Presov where the Slovak Soviet Republic was declared on 16 June 1919

wars.outcome: Hungarian Red Army advance into the north in June 1919 (Slovak Soviet Republic, 16 June); cease-fire of 1 July 1919 and withdrawal; no territory kept.
wars.note: The Trianon page dates only the cease-fire; the 16 June declaration at Presov is from the Hungarian-Romanian War page.

wars.name: Slovak-Hungarian War
wars.outcome: A short war after the occupation of Carpathian Ruthenia; Hungary gained 1,897 km2 with 69,630 inhabitants in eastern Slovakia ('the March 27-April 4 negotiations'), and was halted under German pressure.
wars.note: The First Vienna Award page dates the start: Hungary 'on March 23 launched a larger attack on eastern Slovakia' (re-read 2026-11-01); the negotiations ran 'March 27 - April 4' and gave Hungary 1,897 km2. The page gives no ceasefire date. The Slovak State has its own dossier (slovak-republic).

wars.name: Axis invasion of Yugoslavia

zones.text: Backa (Vojvodina), Baranja, Medjimurje (Murakoz) and the north-eastern Prekmurje

wars.outcome: Yugoslavia invaded on 6 April 1941 and capitulated on 17 April; Hungary annexed Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje and Prekmurje.
wars.note: The Axis occupation page gives no date for the Hungarian annexation; the Hungarian occupation page (read in the fix pass) gives 'The occupation began on 11 April 1941 when 80,000 Hungarian troops crossed the Yugoslav border' and 'Annexed by Hungary: 14 December 1941' (Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje, Prekmurje).

wars.name: Soviet conquest of Hungary

zones.text: Hungary and the lands regained 1938-1941, as of 1943

wars.outcome: The Red Army (with Romanian troops) crossed the border in September 1944, encircled Budapest on 29 December 1944 and took it on 13 February 1945; an armistice was signed in Moscow on 20 January 1945 and the last German troops were expelled on 4 April 1945.
wars.note: The page names the dates; it does not describe an Allied Control Commission.

certainty.note: Czechoslovak, Romanian and Serbian forces were advancing and the Romanian army occupied the east and Budapest in 1919; no line was fixed.
Trianon (1920), the Burgenland settlement (1921) and the First Vienna Award (2 November 1938) are treaty or arbitration lines.

The annexations of Carpathian Ruthenia (March 1939), eastern Slovakia (April 1939) and Backa (1941) followed invasions and the Second Vienna Award (30 August 1940) was an arbitration; the pages give no survey lines.
The frontier of 1 January 1938 that the 1947 Paris treaty confirmed; the de facto lines of 1945 are not on the pages.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Hungarian Republic' row (1919-1943, Wikipedia field 'Hungary', Q28) is the Hungary of the regency: it was a republic only in 1918-1919 and a kingdom from 29 February 1920 to 1 February 1946, so the dossier carries the republic and the soviet republic as 'rename' events inside one state and is named by years. The Wikidata id Q28513 shared with 'Hungarian Nationalists' and 'Austria-Hungary' belongs to other rows (1848-1849, 1868-1918); the 1947 'Hungary' row is a separate dossier (hungary, from 1989; the Second Hungarian Republic, February 1946 - August 1949, is second-hungarian-republic). Not on the pages opened: the date of the Hungarian Democratic Republic's proclamation (November 1918), the Hungarian entry into Backa and the other districts in April 1941, the Soviet occupation and Allied Control Commission of 1944-1947, the 20 January 1945 armistice, and the December 1921 handover dates of Burgenland. The 1919 shape (119,603 km2) is adjusted to the rump; 1918 is borrowed. Counterparts needing a dossier: slovak-republic (the Slovak State, 1939-1945, eu-21 additions) and 'Carpatho-Ukraine' (14-15 March 1939). The Trianon transfer to Poland of northern Arva and Szepes (a 1920 arbitration) is a Czechoslovak loss, not a Hungarian one, and is not recorded here. Dating of losses to Romania and Czechoslovakia follows Trianon (June 1920); the Romanian dossier records its gains at the unions of 1918 and its Czechoslovak counterpart records Ruthenia in April 1919. Pages: seven are cited (five budget plus two shared with the Yugoslav and Romanian batches whose pages were already open).

Fix pass after review eu-21-b (2026-11-01). Applied: (1) the Romanian contest and occupation regions of 1919-1920 (ledger and war zone) now lie in Hungary: the east-of-Tisza counties for the contest, the post-Trianon territory minus a Lake Balaton disc for the occupation; the earlier spec (1919 shape minus 1920 shape) landed in Slovakia and Ruthenia (116 cells, none in Romania); the Csongrad and Jasz-Nagykun-Szolnok parts east of the river are left out of the contest. (2) The Slovak-Hungarian War start is month 3, confidence 2 (First Vienna Award page: 'on March 23 launched a larger attack on eastern Slovakia'), applied by the reviewer; the war note is corrected. (3) Month of the 1941 annexation: 4 (occupation began 11 April 1941; formal annexation 14 December 1941, Hungarian occupation page). (4) The 1944 loss of Yugoslav land is split: Backa and Baranja to the Partisans (October 1944) and Medjimurje and Prekmurje to Yugoslavia (1945). (5) The German occupation ends 4 April 1945 (Hungary in World War II page) and the Soviet conquest (September 1944 - 4 April 1945) and occupation are now events and a war. Not changed: the 1945 loss of southern Slovakia and Ruthenia (/ledger 1945, confidence 1): no page opened dates it; czechoslovakia books the strip from slovak-republic, so the mirror must be fixed there. Disagreement with the reviewer's matrix: none. Dating difference left: the nazi-germany dossier ends its occupation in May 1945, this one on 4 April (page).
